solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Couple that dances around cooler (6)

indicatorNotes.dances: the letters of THAT dance about, stepping into a new order
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go round the cooler, enclosing it

blocks.note: THAT rearranged, split ATT…H
AC = air conditioning, a cooler

annotation.surface: A pair take to the dance floor and circle the drinks cooler.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Couple' reads as a noun, two dancers, but the definition is the verb: to couple is to join.
annotation.definitionFit: Couple as a verb, to join one thing to another as railway wagons are coupled, is a plain synonym of attach.

entries.clue: You shouldn’t have pain often in hand bones (5)

blocks.note: what you say when given a present: thanks, TA
repetitive strain injury, a common pain in the hand and wrist

annotation.surface: A warning that painful hand bones mean you have been overdoing something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hand bones' runs together on the surface, yet the hand belongs to RSI and the tarsi are in the foot. TA is British informal for thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the bones of the ankle and upper foot, so 'bones' is a plain plural definition.

entries.clue: Burden of Scottish political party beginning to take on region there (9)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: only the beginning of 'take', its first letter, is used

blocks.note: the Alba Party, a Scottish nationalist party
first letter of Take
Ross, a region of the Scottish Highlands; 'there' points back to Scotland

annotation.surface: A small Scottish party saddled with taking on a whole region.
annotation.walkthrough: Alba is also the Gaelic name for Scotland. The albatross as burden comes from the Ancient Mariner, who had to wear the bird he shot.
annotation.definitionFit: From Coleridge's poem, an albatross round your neck is a figurative burden you cannot shed.

entries.clue: Female accepting program’s result (6)

indicatorNotes.accepting: HEN accepts APP the way a host accepts a guest, taking it inside

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird
an app is a program; the 's is the clue's grammar

annotation.surface: A woman takes on the program's findings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Result' reads as a noun, the outcome of the program, but here it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Result as a verb, to come about as a consequence, is a plain synonym of happen.

entries.clue: Guy stuck in pile of earth, perhaps sinking fast (8)

indicatorNotes.stuck in: RIB is stuck in MOUND, lodged inside it

blocks.note: to guy and to rib both mean to tease
a mound is a pile of earth

annotation.surface: A man trapped in a heap of soil, maybe going under quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is a man on the surface and a verb in the wordplay: to guy someone is to mock them, to rib them.
annotation.definitionFit: Moribund means close to death, and a patient sinking fast is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

entries.clue: Me? I’m a tradesman, I cast traditional organs etc (10,5)

indicatorNotes.cast: the letters are thrown into a new shape, as metal is cast in a mould

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A craftsman introduces himself as someone who casts old-fashioned organs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organs' conjures church organs being cast in a foundry; here they are organs of the press, newspapers and broadcasters.
annotation.definitionFit: Newspapers and broadcasters are organs of opinion, and the established ones make up the mainstream media.

entries.clue: Concerning American serving drink, not quite removing the head (8)

indicatorNotes.not quite: the drink is not quite complete, so it loses its last letter

blocks.note: re = concerning
a GI is an American soldier, one serving
CIDER without its last letter

annotation.surface: A barman serving an American a drink, skimming off the froth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Removing the head' sounds like pouring off a beer's foam; the head is the head of state, the monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: Regicide is the killing of a king, removing the nation's head in a figurative sense.

entries.clue: One maybe seeking belt for dog (5)

blocks.note: a title belt is the prize in prizefighting, so this is someone who fights for one
a German breed of dog, square-jawed and muscular

annotation.surface: Someone looking for a belt to use as a dog lead.
annotation.walkthrough: The belt is a championship belt, not something to hold up trousers or lead a dog.
annotation.definitionFit: A boxer competes for title belts, and the boxer is also a German breed of dog.

entries.clue: Primitive entering 22.5 degrees west in good condition (6-3)

indicatorNotes.entering: EARLY enters NNEW, going inside it as someone enters a room

blocks.note: north-north-east lies 22.5 degrees round from north
primitive = early, as in early man
W = west

annotation.surface: Something primitive heading off on a compass bearing, still in good shape.
annotation.walkthrough: The number looks like geometry, but it is a compass bearing: the sixteen compass points are 22.5 degrees apart. The hyphenated answer splits its letters differently from the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Nearly-new is the second-hand trade's term for goods barely used and still in good condition.

entries.clue: Period when Reform sought gin bar as PR exercise (4,6)

indicatorNotes.exercise: the letters are put through their paces and come out in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Reform UK, the British party, promoting itself with a gin bar.
annotation.walkthrough: Reform looks like the name of the British political party; here it is the reform protesters sought across the Arab world from 2010.
annotation.definitionFit: The Arab Spring was the period of uprisings in which people across the Arab world demanded reform.

entries.clue: Look into artist cutting axes (1-3)

indicatorNotes.cutting: RA cuts into XY, as a blade cuts between two things

blocks.note: the x and y axes of a graph
RA = Royal Academician, an artist

annotation.surface: Investigating an artist who hacks with axes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Axes' invites choppers; it is the plural of axis, the x and y of a graph.
annotation.definitionFit: An X-ray image lets a doctor see inside the body, so to X-ray is literally to look into something.

entries.clue: Harrow from Germany is kept in trim (8)

indicatorNotes.kept in: IST is kept in DRESS as something is kept in a box, held inside it

blocks.note: to dress is to trim, as in dressing a hedge or a shop window
ist is the German for is

annotation.surface: An agricultural harrow imported from Germany and kept in good order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harrow' is the farm tool on the surface and a verb in the answer; it is not the London school.
annotation.definitionFit: Harrow as a verb, to torment someone's feelings, is a plain synonym of distress.

entries.clue: Turn around, facing barrier in the East End (6)

blocks.note: c = circa, around
HURDLE with the H dropped, as in a Cockney accent

annotation.surface: Someone spinning round to face a barricade in east London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn around' reads as one instruction; 'Turn' alone is the definition, as milk turns. The East End of London is the home of Cockney, which drops its h's.
annotation.definitionFit: Milk that turns goes sour and curdles, so turn is used in its dairy sense.

entries.clue: Result of mischief found in Pandora’s box (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the following words, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: pandorA'S BOx

annotation.surface: The troubles released from Pandora's box in the Greek myth.
annotation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a court order against nuisance behaviour.
annotation.definitionFit: An ASBO was imposed on someone for persistent antisocial mischief, so it is the result of mischief.

entries.clue: Result of tie, both sides leaving keeper up? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.both sides leaving: both sides of the word leave, so its first and last letters go
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ASCOT, a broad neck tie, without its first and last letters
a warder is a prison keeper; 'up' reverses it

annotation.surface: A drawn cup tie in which both teams scored and a goalkeeper was left stranded.
annotation.walkthrough: The football picture pushes 'keeper' towards the goalkeeper and 'tie' towards a cup match; the tie is an ascot, a cravat, and the keeper guards a prison.
annotation.definitionFit: A score draw is a drawn match in which both sides scored, a key result on British football pools coupons.

entries.clue: Star laughing about Ed Gamble’s opener (3,5)

indicatorNotes.about: RIANT goes about ED and G, surrounding them
indicatorNotes.opener: the opener of a word is its first letter, G of Gamble

blocks.note: riant is a literary word for laughing
used literally
first letter of Gamble

annotation.surface: A celebrity chuckling at the comedian Ed Gamble's opening joke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star' and Ed Gamble, a British comedian, make a showbusiness picture, but the star is astronomical.
annotation.definitionFit: A red giant is a type of star, large and cool, late in its life, so this is a definition by class.

entries.clue: Secretly conspiring South American is having a laugh (2,7)

blocks.note: the Inca people of Peru
to hoot is to laugh loudly

annotation.surface: A South American plotting in secret while laughing about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having a laugh' is British for joking; here it is simply laughing, HOOTS.
annotation.definitionFit: People in cahoots are in league, working together in secret, which is the idiom's meaning.

entries.clue: Trial tried to avoid electronic transfer (8)

indicatorNotes.to avoid: HEARD must avoid E, steering clear of it, so the E is left out

blocks.note: HEARD (a case is heard, tried) without E for electronic
to ship is to transfer goods

annotation.surface: A court case where someone tried to dodge an electronic money transfer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trial' and 'tried' set up a courtroom; the definition is trial as an ordeal.
annotation.definitionFit: Trial in the sense of an ordeal or affliction, not a court case, is a plain synonym of hardship.

entries.clue: Unfinished sweet dish otherwise called savoury dish (8)

indicatorNotes.Unfinished: the sweet dish is left unfinished, so MOUSSE loses its last letter

blocks.note: MOUSSE without its last letter
aka = also known as

annotation.surface: A half-eaten pudding that goes by another name, a savoury one.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue sets a sweet dish against a savoury one; the second 'dish' is a separate word, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a savoury Greek bake of aubergine and minced meat, defined here by its class.

entries.clue: Habit of constant predator (4)

blocks.note: c is the constant for the speed of light
an owl is a bird of prey

annotation.surface: The regular habit of a hunter that never stops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Habit' is a routine on the surface, and a monk's garment in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A cowl is the hooded robe worn by a monk, and habit is the word for a monk's dress.

entries.clue: Imperative model of chivalry? (6)

blocks.note: imperative as an adjective: pressing, demanding action now
UR- (original, from German) + GENT: the original gentleman

annotation.surface: A commanding figure who is the very pattern of good manners.
annotation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits UR-GENT: the German prefix ur- means original, as in Urtext, so an ur-gent is the first gentleman, the model for all others.
annotation.definitionFit: Imperative and urgent share the sense of demanding immediate action; the second sense is a punning coinage.

entries.clue: Tail-enders from England side, of the eleven, needed support (6)

indicatorNotes.Tail-enders: tail-enders are those at the end, so the last letters of the following words are taken

blocks.clueFragment: England side, of the eleven, needed
blocks.note: englanD sidE oF thE eleveN needeD

annotation.surface: England's lower-order cricketers were needed to save the match.
annotation.walkthrough: Tail-enders are the weakest batsmen in a cricket side, who bat last, and here they are the last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Defend and support share the sense of backing a person or cause against attack.

entries.clue: US symbol for 3 + 1, of course (5)

blocks.note: the national bird on the Great Seal of the United States
3 is the answer to 3 Down, a golf score of three under par; one more stroke gives the next score up, on a golf course

annotation.surface: An American emblem for a sum that everyone knows.
annotation.walkthrough: 3 is the answer to 3 Down, ALBATROSS: on a golf course an albatross is three under par, and one stroke more is an eagle, two under.
annotation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is the national bird of the United States, and an eagle is two under par on a golf hole.

entries.clue: Who hopes to profit from French sea air? (8)

blocks.note: mer is French for sea
an air is a tune, a chant

annotation.surface: Someone wanting to cash in on bottled sea breezes from France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Air' is a sea breeze on the surface and a tune in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A merchant buys and sells in the hope of making a profit, so the definition describes the trade.

entries.clue: State promoting independence initially in revolutionary rule (5)

indicatorNotes.promoting: promoting raises something in rank, so the I moves up the down entry
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: something revolutionary revolves, turning right round, so REIGN is read backwards

blocks.note: to reign is to rule
first letter of independence, promoted one place in NGIER

annotation.surface: A country pushing for independence under a revolutionary regime.
annotation.walkthrough: Turned round, REIGN gives NGIER; promoting the I, moving it higher in this down entry, gives NIGER.
annotation.definitionFit: Niger is an independent West African country, and state here means a nation.

entries.clue: 21 regressing without A & E? (4)

indicatorNotes.regressing: to regress is to go backwards, so GUARD is read in reverse
indicatorNotes.without: without means lacking, so the A is left out

blocks.note: 21 Across is DEFEND, which is to guard
used literally, and removed

annotation.surface: Someone backing away from Accident and Emergency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A & E' reads as the hospital casualty department, but it splits: A is removed, and E, ecstasy, is the example the answer defines.
annotation.definitionFit: E is short for ecstasy, a recreational drug; the question mark flags a definition by example.

entries.clue: Mongrel dog hoped for one returning dog’s dinner to Labrador (10)

indicatorNotes.Mongrel: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the letters are mixed
indicatorNotes.returning: EG returns, going back the way it came, so it reads GE

blocks.note: anagram fodder
eg = for example, for one

annotation.surface: A mutt hoping a Labrador will hand back some of its dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: The Labrador is not a dog but the region of Canada: hodgepodge is the North American form of the British hotchpotch, and a dog's dinner is British slang for a mess.
annotation.definitionFit: A hodgepodge is a jumbled mess, what a British speaker calls a dog's dinner, and the word is the North American form.

entries.clue: Short trip on vacation to probe ocean bed feature? (5,3)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: TRIP is vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters
indicatorNotes.to probe: a probe goes inside, so the letters go inside SEA

blocks.note: wee = small, short
TRIP emptied of its middle
the sea is the ocean

annotation.surface: A quick dive during a holiday to investigate the seabed.
annotation.walkthrough: The bed is a flowerbed, not the ocean floor the surface paints; the question mark signals a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a scented climbing flower grown in garden beds, an example of a bed feature.

entries.clue: Head of security again took back shocking equipment (6)

indicatorNotes.Head of: the head of a word is its first letter, S of security
indicatorNotes.back: the letters are taken back, read from right to left

blocks.note: first letter of Security
resat = sat again, as with an exam

annotation.surface: A security chief retook the kit the guards use.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Took back' reads as reclaimed; 'took' belongs with 'again' as RESAT, an exam taken again, and 'back' reverses the lot.
annotation.definitionFit: Tasers are electroshock weapons, so 'shocking' is literal here rather than meaning scandalous.
